## William W. L. Cheung

I am a Professor at the University of British Columbia and Canada Research Chair in Ocean Sustainability and Global Change. My research examines how climate change is transforming marine ecosystems, fisheries, aquatic food systems, and ocean-dependent societies.

I develop and apply interdisciplinary models, scenarios, and assessment approaches to understand climate risks and identify pathways toward sustainable, equitable, and resilient ocean futures.

My work spans research, training, knowledge mobilization, and international science-policy assessment, including contributions to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES).

## Research approach

My work connects marine ecology, fisheries science, climate-impact assessment, economics, scenarios, and governance. I am particularly interested in understanding how changes in ocean conditions interact with biodiversity, food systems, institutions, and societal choices.

A central goal of my research is to produce knowledge that is scientifically rigorous, useful for decision-making, and attentive to sustainability and equity.

## Current roles

- Professor, Institute for the Oceans and Fisheries, University of British Columbia
- Canada Research Chair in Ocean Sustainability and Global Change
- Principal Investigator, Changing Ocean Research Unit
- Coordinating Lead Author, IPCC Working Group II Seventh Assessment Report
- Coordinating Lead Author, IPBES Biodiversity and Climate Change Assessment
- Associate Editor, *Global Change Biology*

## Research community

I lead the [Changing Ocean Research Unit](https://coru.oceans.ubc.ca), where students, postdoctoral researchers, and collaborators study climate change, marine biodiversity, fisheries, blue food systems, and pathways toward sustainable ocean futures.

## Honours and recognition

My work has been recognized through election as a Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada and an honorary doctorate from Institut Agro Rennes-Angers.

A fuller account of appointments, honours, publications, and professional activities will be available through my curriculum vitae.
